title: Heat Pump Tax Credits | Inflation Reduction ACT 🔥💰
summary: A Colorado HVAC company explains the 2024 Inflation Reduction Act heat pump credit (30% up to $2,000 a year), the uncapped geothermal credit and cold-climate qualification, and recommends pairing heat pumps with solar.

assertions.quote: for your traditional air source heat pumps it's a $2,000 annual cap
technically these heat pump tax credits based on the bill that was signed are available through 2033
the geothermal heat pump credit is actually 30% annually with no annual cap
the reason geothermal is so much more expensive is because you actually have to drill Loops
if you don't have a tax liability for the year there's no tax benefit to putting in any of this equipment

verdicts.note: 25C was a nonrefundable credit with no carryforward, limited to the taxpayer's liability.

assertions.quote: what you're actually comparing is the cost of natural gas which historically has been very low
the other way that you can almost guarantee you save money is by putting in solar panels
remember a heat pump is just an air conditioner with a reversing valve so a heat pump is also your air conditioner
on average we see about a 30 or 40% savings it is very drastic

verdicts.note: Moving from SEER 13 to a high-SEER inverter unit can cut cooling energy roughly 25-40% on paper, but measured savings are often smaller.
In MA, a cooling-only central heat pump replacing existing central AC saves only about 69 kWh per ton a year and is not cost-effective (benefit-cost 0.14); hotter climates may differ.
